note: All five modes from one Do over one drone, a Scale selector in every block: Lydian, major, Mixolydian, Dorian (one note lowered each time), then Dorian, natural minor, Phrygian, Locrian, then one made-up phrase in four modes on a new Do. The major and natural minor scales are in the chain because Lydian to Mixolydian and Dorian to Phrygian are two notes apart without them. Each selector is invited with a feel, never a chip. The Scale selector is the lesson, so the file has no moves: the last block's new Do is its second key. Missing: a staff highlight that follows the choice (the staff rings the three notes that move in a block, not only the one that just moved).

exercise.title: Five modes from one Do
exercise.why: From one Do the modes stand in a line where each is the one before it with one note lowered a half step, so singing down that line over one drone lets you hear each mode by the single note that moved.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. The staff holds the Lydian mode. Sing it up from the low {{1}} to the next {{1}} and back down. Sing it on "oo".
The three ringed notes are the ones that move in this block: {{#4}}, {{7}} and {{3}}. Once you hear them against the drone, go on to the next scale. Use the Scale selector below to change the scale, then press Start exercise to start the drone again.
When you change the scale, one ringed note drops a half step and the rest stay: {{#4}} to {{4}} for the major scale, {{7}} to {{b7}} for Mixolydian, {{3}} to {{b3}} for Dorian.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together. The staff holds the Dorian mode again, where the last block ended. Sing it up from the low {{1}} to the next {{1}} and back down. Sing it on "oo".
The three ringed notes are the ones that move now: {{6}}, {{2}} and {{5}}. Once you hear them against the drone, go on to the next scale. Use the Scale selector below to change the scale, then press Start exercise to start the drone again.
When you change the scale, one ringed note drops a half step and the rest stay: {{6}} to {{b6}} for the natural minor scale, {{2}} to {{b2}} for Phrygian, {{5}} to {{b5}} for Locrian.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, on a new {{1}}, in the Lydian mode. Make up a short phrase that climbs from the low {{1}} towards the next {{1}} and comes back to end on {{1}}. Sing it on "la".
Once the phrase comes back the same each time, sing it in another mode. Use the Scale selector below to change the scale, then press Start exercise to start the drone again.
When you change the scale, the drone and {{1}} stay, and the phrase keeps its shape while some of its notes move a half step.
